areas.rationale: Keep the provider-neutral API and its generated contracts in one removable product-owned boundary.
semantic_invariants: The API remains provider-neutral and cannot depend on TraceDecay host internals.
Generated contract bindings remain derived from the versioned provider contract set.

upstreamability.rationale: The provider-neutral contract can be proposed independently without carrying any concrete provider implementation.

areas.rationale: Keep routing, admission, and provider-neutral lifecycle behavior outside every concrete adapter and upstream host crate.
semantic_invariants: The fabric routes capabilities without branching on concrete provider names.
Unavailable providers remain typed failures and never trigger silent fallback.

upstreamability.rationale: The provider-neutral fabric is separable from product adapters and can converge through its public contracts.

areas.rationale: Own provider construction and activation outside the host while exposing one typed project-scoped composition object.
semantic_invariants: Disabled activation constructs no fabric, provider, storage, queue, or background worker.
Enabled Native activation requires the canonical application port explicitly.

upstreamability.rationale: Product selection and construction policy stays removable behind the narrow host composition mount.

areas.rationale: Adapt canonical Native application operations without moving Native persistence authority into the provider layer.
semantic_invariants: The adapter delegates all canonical effects through the injected Native application port.
Provider terminals cannot claim effects that the Native application port did not report.

upstreamability.rationale: The adapter remains product-owned while Native storage and application authority stay unchanged upstream.

areas.rationale: Isolate NCM protocol mapping, audit evidence, and fail-closed readiness from provider-neutral and host code.
semantic_invariants: NCM receives only opaque exact-scope namespaces and bounded provider requests.
NCM cannot become production-ready without verified identity, limits, and readiness proof.

upstreamability.rationale: The licensed external-provider adapter and its evidence remain isolated from the upstream host architecture.

areas.rationale: Keep black-box provider conformance, dummy-provider fixtures, and product host journeys in one observer-isolated test boundary.
semantic_invariants: Observer reports contain structural outcomes and never retain provider payload bytes.
Differential runs compare full identity, terminal, effect, and retained outcome semantics.

upstreamability.rationale: Provider-neutral conformance behavior can be upstreamed independently from product provider implementations.

areas.rationale: Reserve a product-owned normalized observation boundary before any observer implementation is admitted.
semantic_invariants: Planned observation paths grant no classification authority until the area becomes active.
Canonical host ingest remains independent from provider delivery and provider failure.

upstreamability.rationale: The reserved provider-neutral observation seam can converge only after behavioral implementation exists.

areas.rationale: Reserve the product-owned context compiler without claiming an absent implementation as active capability.
semantic_invariants: Planned context paths grant no classification authority until the compiler is implemented.
TraceDecay remains authority for final context assembly and current code truth.

upstreamability.rationale: The reserved provider-neutral compiler can converge only after its substantive behavior and tests exist.

areas.rationale: Own product planning, architecture evidence, upstream policy, checkers, tests, and isolated workflows outside upstream crates.
semantic_invariants: Governance artifacts never authorize an upstream edit without one exact active entry.
Computed counts remain runtime output and are not copied into stored snapshots or receipts.

upstreamability.rationale: Product planning and convergence enforcement remain downstream-owned while preserving upstream identity explicitly.

areas.rationale: Track the two upstream-owned root workspace files separately from every additive product crate.
semantic_invariants: Workspace edits register only additive product-owned crates and their generated resolution.
The pinned toolchain regenerates Cargo.lock without unrelated dependency version changes.

upstreamability.rationale: Workspace membership can be removed directly and the lockfile is regenerated from the remaining manifests.

areas.rationale: Track the exact default-off host feature, project composition, retained ownership proof, and MCP construction seam as one removable mount.
semantic_invariants: Disabled composition creates no provider registry, adapter, storage, queue, or background work.
The provider host mount is retained and retired with exactly one cached project server.
No concrete provider implementation leaks into MCP routes or public host contracts.

upstreamability.rationale: These five exact files form the smallest current host patch and can be removed with the optional feature.

areas.rationale: Constrain the five existing daemon shutdown layers that must share one caller deadline and expose incomplete blocking drain truthfully.
semantic_invariants: Upstream behavior: daemon shutdown preserves lifecycle ordering and always completes terminal teardown after reporting the observed outcome.
Product behavior: one caller-supplied absolute deadline bounds every nested shutdown and blocking-drain step without refresh.

upstreamability.rationale: The absolute-deadline shutdown correction is provider-neutral and can converge independently as an upstream lifecycle fix.

areas.rationale: Constrain the two existing integration-test harness paths that select the checkout CLI and isolate daemon routing for memory-suite execution.
semantic_invariants: Upstream behavior: integration tests use one bounded production-equivalent daemon socket and never inherit an installed daemon or global profile.
Product behavior: the memory suite executes a CLI built from the same checkout or fails closed before mixing revisions.

upstreamability.rationale: Deterministic same-checkout integration-test isolation is provider-neutral and can be proposed upstream without product runtime changes.

entries.rationale: Record deterministic resolution for the additive product-owned workspace crates and optional host dependency.
semantic_invariants: Cargo.lock is regenerated by the pinned Cargo toolchain and is never hand-edited.
Existing unrelated package versions and checksums remain unchanged by product path packages.
entries.rebase_or_removal_plan: Regenerate Cargo.lock after removing product workspace members and retain every unrelated upstream resolution.

upstreamability.rationale: The lockfile delta is reproduced from pinned manifests and disappears when their path packages are removed.

entries.rationale: Register the additive provider API, fabric, adapters, registry, and conformance crates in the existing virtual workspace.
semantic_invariants: Workspace membership remains additive and does not change upstream default features.
Removing the product crate member lines restores the upstream workspace manifest.
entries.rebase_or_removal_plan: Remove only the additive product workspace member lines while preserving every upstream workspace setting.

upstreamability.rationale: The additive member list can be proposed upstream independently or removed without changing host behavior.

entries.rationale: Declare one optional registry dependency and product host feature at the TraceDecay package boundary.

The host package depends only on the provider registry and never on a concrete adapter.
entries.rebase_or_removal_plan: Remove the optional dependency, memory-provider-host feature, and its feature-list membership together.

upstreamability.rationale: The optional dependency is the single package-level bridge and can be upstreamed or deleted independently.

entries.rationale: Compose one disabled provider host after cache misses and retain it across both MCP construction paths.
semantic_invariants: Disabled activation constructs no provider infrastructure or background work.
The mount is created once per project server and reused across retained construction paths.
entries.rebase_or_removal_plan: Remove the typed mount helper, disabled activation, and two construction-context injections as one bounded patch.

upstreamability.rationale: The project composition seam is explicit, default-off, and independent from provider implementation details.

entries.rationale: Prove disabled host inertness, cache identity retention, and shutdown release at the existing ownership journey.
semantic_invariants: Every alias and cache hit retains the identical project-scoped host mount.
Project shutdown releases the host mount with the cached project server ownership cycle.
entries.rebase_or_removal_plan: Remove only the feature-gated mount identity, inertness, and release assertions with the host mount.

upstreamability.rationale: The ownership proof documents the host lifecycle contract and can accompany the minimal mount upstream.

entries.rationale: Retain the opaque provider host mount for exactly the cached MCP project-server lifetime.
semantic_invariants: MCP routes never inspect or branch on concrete provider implementations.
The retained mount has no authority over source, sessions, tools, or Native storage.
entries.rebase_or_removal_plan: Remove the feature-gated retained field, constructor transfer, and test accessor without changing MCP routes.

upstreamability.rationale: One opaque retained field is the smallest server-lifetime ownership bridge for the composition object.

entries.rationale: Carry the opaque project provider composition through existing MCP construction contexts without exposing adapter types.
semantic_invariants: Construction defaults remain empty when the optional host feature is absent.
The construction context carries only the registry composition boundary and no provider-specific route state.
entries.rebase_or_removal_plan: Remove the feature-gated type alias, optional construction field, defaults, and builder method together.

upstreamability.rationale: The optional construction field is a bounded transport for project ownership and can be removed atomically.

entries.rationale: Seed daemon shutdown with the caller's absolute deadline so lower layers consume one bounded budget rather than independent timeouts.
semantic_invariants: Upstream behavior: daemon bootstrap preserves its existing shutdown sequence and terminal cleanup responsibilities.
Product behavior: bootstrap passes one caller-owned absolute deadline into the engine without refreshing its budget.
entries.rebase_or_removal_plan: Drop the deadline argument only if upstream daemon shutdown already exposes and propagates an equivalent absolute-deadline contract.

upstreamability.rationale: The bootstrap handoff is a provider-neutral correctness fix that can be upstreamed with the shutdown deadline chain.

entries.rationale: Carry the caller's deadline through engine shutdown so project runtime teardown cannot receive a newly extended budget.
semantic_invariants: Upstream behavior: engine shutdown retains its current ownership and teardown ordering across managed project runtimes.
Product behavior: the engine forwards the unchanged absolute deadline to every nested shutdown operation.
entries.rebase_or_removal_plan: Remove the engine forwarding delta when upstream engine shutdown accepts the same caller-owned absolute deadline.

upstreamability.rationale: The engine signature and forwarding change are the narrow upstream bridge for deadline conservation.

entries.rationale: Forward the shared deadline through invocation shutdown to LSP and project-runtime owners without extending either nested operation.
semantic_invariants: Upstream behavior: invocation-state teardown continues to retire LSP and project-runtime resources in the established order.
Product behavior: invocation-state shutdown forwards one unchanged deadline and reports any incomplete nested teardown.
entries.rebase_or_removal_plan: Remove the invocation-state forwarding patch after upstream accepts an equivalent shared-deadline shutdown signature.

upstreamability.rationale: The invocation-state bridge preserves upstream authority while closing the nested deadline-refresh gap.

entries.rationale: Bound LSP shutdown by the remaining caller budget so process teardown cannot silently outlive the daemon's absolute deadline.
semantic_invariants: Upstream behavior: LSP teardown retains its existing process ownership and reports the real shutdown outcome.
Product behavior: LSP shutdown consumes only the remaining shared deadline and never creates a fresh timeout.
entries.rebase_or_removal_plan: Delete the local LSP deadline adaptation when upstream LSP shutdown consumes the caller's absolute deadline directly.

upstreamability.rationale: Bounded LSP teardown is an upstream daemon-lifecycle correction independent of memory-provider behavior.

entries.rationale: Bound blocking project-runtime drain by the shared deadline, expose incomplete drain as Failed, and still perform terminal teardown.
semantic_invariants: Upstream behavior: project-runtime shutdown reaches terminal teardown and truthfully reports an incomplete blocking drain as Failed.
Product behavior: blocking drain is bounded by the caller deadline and cannot extend shutdown through an internal replacement budget.
entries.rebase_or_removal_plan: Remove the bounded-drain implementation when upstream project-runtime shutdown provides the same deadline conservation and truthful terminal outcome.

upstreamability.rationale: Bounded blocking drain and truthful failure reporting are provider-neutral upstream lifecycle fixes.

semantic_invariants: Upstream behavior: the common harness isolates daemon socket and profile state without changing production command behavior.
Product behavior: integration tests use an explicit or Cargo-provided same-checkout CLI and fail closed instead of guessing sibling binaries.

entries.rebase_or_removal_plan: Remove the local harness resolver and isolation helpers when upstream provides equivalent fail-closed same-checkout command construction.
